scope: ELR-SEC-106 only: trusted report, block, and unblock operations; their atomic audit events; per-actor quotas; and the directly related Firestore read/write boundaries.
scopeLimit: This is not an application-wide security or Android V1 release score. Server-side Claim, resumable account deletion, fan voting, disputes, public/private player profile separation, App Check rollout, deployment, and Android device release gates remain open under later tickets.

candidate.note: Verification applies to the current local candidate layered on this base revision; it is not evidence of a committed or deployed release.

target.verificationSource: Repository configuration and local Firebase Functions, Auth, Firestore, and Storage emulators. No production mutation or deployment was attempted.

summary: Report, block, and unblock are authenticated callables with no client write fallback. Each successful state transition, its bounded opaque audit event, and its per-actor quota update are staged in one Firestore transaction. Directional mutual blocks remain independent, duplicate retries are neutral and do not consume quota, deleted-account tombstones invalidate still-cached tokens, canonical friendship paths resist client poisoning, and legacy relationship arrays are repaired without discarding valid mutual blocks. Functions unit, final Functions/Auth/Firestore/Storage Emulator smoke, Rules Emulator, focused Flutter, analysis, architecture and index gates pass on the local candidate.

evidence: reportUserContent derives reporterId from Auth, validates the target and payload, and creates the private report plus trusted audit in one transaction
the transaction requires an active reporter profile and no account-deletion tombstone, so a cached token cannot report after deletion starts
report audit uses moderationReport plus an opaque report ID and excludes targetId, reason, details, names, and relationship arrays
repeating the same daily report returns a neutral duplicate result without another report, audit event, or quota operation
blockUser and unblockUser derive the actor from Auth and transact both player documents, the friendship, the quota, and the audit event together
each direction has independent blockedIds state, so one user's unblock cannot erase the opposite user's block
the stored friendship participants must match the canonical actor-target pair before mutation, preventing underscore-ID collisions from overwriting or deleting another relationship
legacy friendIds and blockedIds are normalized for both players in the transaction while every valid bounded ID and the opposite directional block are preserved
duplicate block and unblock calls repair legacy state without consuming quota or creating an audit event; an audit failure rolls every transition repair back
an actor-scoped window revision makes block, unblock, then block in the same millisecond produce three unique immutable audit events
new profile reports are capped at 20 per actor per UTC day
block and unblock transitions share a cap of 30 per actor per hour
quota counters are backend-only, live at safetyActionQuotas/{uid}, are removed by the current account-deletion cleanup, and duplicate no-op calls consume no quota
Firestore Rules deny every client read and write to userReports, safetyActionQuotas, and accountDeletionRequests and deny direct auditEvents writes
clients cannot change blockedIds or create, update, or delete a blocked friendship
client friendship creation is pending-only on the canonical pair path, acceptance belongs to the receiver, and create or acceptance fails while either participant blocks the other
new non-list or oversized relationship arrays are rejected without preventing unrelated updates to legacy profiles

friendships are readable only by their participants; the production accepted and pending participant queries pass, broad or other-user queries are denied, and safety audit events are readable only by their authenticated actor
Flutter block and unblock paths call CloudSensitiveOpsService and have no local Firestore fallback
Flutter and Functions share the friendships, userReports, safetyActionQuotas, accountDeletionRequests, and auditEvents collection contract
required actor and audit query indexes are present and preserved by the index guard

attackMatrix.attack: unauthenticated caller invokes report, block, or unblock
authenticated client forges or edits userReports, auditEvents, safetyActionQuotas, blockedIds, or a blocked friendship
authenticated caller submits forged reporterId, actorId, or blockerId fields, or targets itself
attackMatrix.expected: derive identity from Auth and reject every self-targeted operation without writes

attackMatrix.attack: deleted actor reuses a still-valid token after its player profile is removed or an account-deletion tombstone exists
attackMatrix.expected: permission-denied before report, relationship, quota, or audit writes

attackMatrix.attack: report or block targets a missing profile
attackMatrix.expected: reject without report, relationship, quota, or audit writes

attackMatrix.attack: free-form report evidence, reason, raw target ID, or relationship arrays leak into Audit
opposite users block each other, retry, and independently unblock
attackMatrix.expected: one event per real directional transition and no erased opposite block

attackMatrix.attack: block, unblock, and block occur with the same millisecond timestamp
attackMatrix.expected: three unique audit IDs and final blocked state

attackMatrix.attack: two different participant pairs collapse to the same underscore-joined friendship document ID
attackMatrix.expected: reject the mismatched stored pair without overwrite, delete, quota, or audit writes

attackMatrix.attack: client creates a friendship under an arbitrary or reversed path, creates it accepted, forges lastActionBy, self-accepts, or creates or accepts while either player blocks the other
attackMatrix.expected: deny while the canonical sender-created pending request and receiver acceptance remain usable

attackMatrix.attack: legacy player data contains missing, scalar, duplicate, mixed, or otherwise malformed friendIds or blockedIds
attackMatrix.expected: preserve every valid bounded ID and mutual block, repair both players atomically, and never let malformed arrays make the target permanently unblockable

attackMatrix.attack: actor exceeds 20 new reports per day or 30 relationship transitions per hour
attackMatrix.expected: resource-exhausted with no partial state or audit write

attackMatrix.attack: outsider reads a friendship or target reads the reporter's safety audit event
client lists friendships without a participant constraint or queries another user's participant scope
attackMatrix.expected: deny while the production accepted and pending participant-scoped queries remain usable

attackMatrix.attack: trusted audit creation fails after domain and quota writes are staged

functionsEmulatorSmoke.coverage: All six auth gates, settlement roster guards, forged identity fields, self-target rejection, concurrent safety retries, opaque audit events, directional unblock, deleted-actor tombstones, quota persistence and cleanup, and the final legacy friendIds/blockedIds repair scenarios passed with exit code 0. Duplicate legacy repairs are asserted to consume no quota and create no audit event.

hotspotGuard.scopeNote: No ELR-SEC-106 file is listed; the seven existing Flutter hotspots remain owned by ELR-OPS-402.

findings.finding: The final blockedIds legacy-repair candidate passed npm run test:functions:emulator with exit code 0 on 2026-08-01.

remainingRisks.risk: Guest Claim remains client-side and account deletion still needs the planned resumable saga before release.
Fan voting and disputes still need trusted callables, atomic transitions, and relationship-scoped reads.
Private player account data still requires migration to a separate public profile projection.

App Check remains later defense in depth under the V1.1 ticket ELR-SEC-701, alongside broader abuse monitoring, moderation SLA, appeals, UGC consent, and youth-safety policy. It is not represented as a current V1 Pilot gate.
The hotspot guard still reports seven existing Flutter production files over budget; none belongs to ELR-SEC-106.

recommendations: Keep all safety state transitions callable-only and preserve the shared quota transaction when extending moderation actions.
Treat App Check as later defense in depth for broader V1.1 social expansion unless Product explicitly reprioritizes it into V1; never treat it as a replacement for authorization or quotas.
Do not expose report text, raw targets, block relationships, quota state, claim tokens, or personal data through audit, analytics, or share links.
Use this 5/5 audit and the reviewed scoped diff as the SEC-106 checkpoint; keep ELR-SEC-107 isolated and do not deploy it before its own independent AppSec and Emulator gates.
releaseDecision: ELR-SEC-106 is DONE locally with a 5/5 scope-limited result: Functions 105/105, final Functions Emulator smoke with six exported callables, Rules 207/207, focused Flutter 12/12, and architecture/index guards passed. Android V1 remains open, the repository candidate is not deployed, and this audit authorizes no Firebase, Remote Config, Hosting, Android, or iOS release.
